en: 'Abbad ibn Musa narrated to me, Ibrahim ibn Sa'd narrated to us, my father informed me, from Muhammad ibn Jubayr ibn Mut'im, from his father, that a woman asked the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) for something and he told her to return to him. She said: "O Messenger of Allah, what if I come and do not find you?" My father said: as if she meant death. He said: "If you do not find me, go to Abu Bakr." And Hajjaj ibn al-Sha'ir narrated it to me, Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from his father, Muhammad ibn Jubayr ibn Mut'im informed me, that his father Jubayr ibn Mut'im informed him that a woman came to the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) and spoke to him about something, and he gave her an instruction... with the like of the hadith of 'Abbad ibn Musa.

And al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Hulwani narrated to me, Ja'far ibn 'Awn narrated to us, from Abu 'Umys; (H) and 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us—and the wording is his—Ja'far ibn 'Awn informed us, Abu 'Umys informed us, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah: I heard 'A'ishah, when she was asked: "Whom would the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) have appointed as successor if he were to appoint a successor?" She said: "Abu Bakr." It was said to her: "Then who after Abu Bakr?" She said: "'Umar." Then it was said to her: "Who after 'Umar?" She said: "Abu 'Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah." Then she stopped at that.

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us, Khalid ibn 'Abdullah informed us, from Khalid, from Abu 'Uthman, 'Amr ibn al-'As informed me that the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) dispatched him as commander of the army of Dhat al-Salasil. I came to him and said: "Which of the people is most beloved to you?" He said: "'A'ishah." I said: "From among the men?" He said: "Her father." I said: "Then who?" He said: "'Umar." And then he enumerated several men.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Abu Mu'awiyah and Waki' narrated to us; (H) and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Jarir informed us; (H) and Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us—all of them from al-A'mash; (H) and Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Numayr and Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us—and the wording is theirs—they said: Waki' narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from 'Abdullah ibn Murrah, from Abu al-Ahwas, from 'Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (pbuh) said: "Behold, I declare myself free before every intimate friend of his intimate friendship. If I were to take an intimate friend, I would have taken Abu Bakr as an intimate friend; indeed, your companion is the intimate friend of Allah."

Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah, Zuhayr ibn Harb, and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us—Ishaq said: informed us, and the others said: narrated to us—Jarir, from Mughirah, from Wasil ibn Hayyan, from 'Abdullah ibn Abi al-Hudhayl, from Abu al-Ahwas, from 'Abdullah, from the Prophet (pbuh), who said: "If I were to take an intimate friend from the people of the earth, I would have taken the son of Abu Quhafah as an intimate friend; but your companion is the intimate friend of Allah."

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar both narrated to us—they said: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to me, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas, from 'Abdullah; (H) and 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us, Ja'far ibn 'Awn informed us, Abu 'Umys informed us, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, from 'Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (pbuh) said: "If I were to take an intimate friend, I would have taken the son of Abu Quhafah as an intimate friend."

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar both narrated to us—and the wording is Ibn al-Muthanna's—they said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas, from 'Abdullah, from the Prophet (pbuh), that he said: "If I were to take anyone from my nation as an intimate friend, I would have taken Abu Bakr."

Muhammad ibn Bashshar al-'Abdi narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Raja', who said: I heard 'Abdullah ibn Abi al-Hudhayl narrating from Abu al-Ahwas, who said: I heard 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud narrating from the Prophet (pbuh) that he said: "If I were to take an intimate friend, I would have taken Abu Bakr as an intimate friend; but he is my brother and my companion, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has taken your companion as an intimate friend."

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me, Ishaq ibn 'Isa narrated to us, Malik narrated to me, from Abu al-Nadr, from 'Amir ibn Sa'd, who said: I heard my father saying: I never heard the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) say of any living person walking that he is in Paradise, except for 'Abdullah ibn Salam.

Sa'id ibn Mansur narrated to us, Fulayh ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Salim Abu al-Nadr, from 'Ubayd ibn Hunayn and Busr ibn Sa'id, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of Allah (pbuh) addressed the people one day... with the like of the hadith of Malik.

Abdullah ibn Ja'far ibn Yahya ibn Khalid narrated to us, Ma'n narrated to us, Malik narrated to us, from Abu al-Nadr, from 'Ubayd ibn Hunayn, from Abu Sa'id, that the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) sat upon the pulpit and said: "A servant was given the choice by Allah between being given the splendor of this world and that which is with Him, and he chose that which is with Him." Thereupon Abu Bakr wept, and wept, and said: "May our fathers and our mothers be ransomed for you!" He said: So the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) was the one who was given the choice, and Abu Bakr was the most knowledgeable of us concerning him. And the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) said: "Indeed, the person who has favored me most in his companionship and his wealth is Abu Bakr. And if I were to take an intimate friend, I would have taken Abu Bakr as an intimate friend; but there is the brotherhood of Islam. Let no small door remain in the mosque except the door of Abu Bakr."

Zuhayr ibn Harb, 'Abd ibn Humayd, and 'Abdullah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Darimi narrated to me—'Abdullah said: informed us, and the other two said: Habban ibn Hilal narrated to us—Hammam narrated to us, Thabit narrated to us, Anas ibn Malik narrated to us, that Abu Bakr al-Siddiq narrated to him, saying: I looked at the feet of the idolaters right above our heads while we were in the cave, and I said: "O Messenger of Allah, if one of them were to look down at his feet, he would see us beneath his feet." He said: "O Abu Bakr, what do you think of two, Allah being the third of them?"

Harmalah ibn Yahya narrated to me, Ibn Wahb informed us, Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, from 'Ubaydullah ibn 'Abdullah ibn 'Utbah ibn Mas'ud, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Abbas, that he and al-Hurr ibn Qays ibn Hisn al-Fazari disputed regarding the companion of Musa (peace be upon him). Ibn 'Abbas said: He is al-Khadir. Ubayy ibn Ka'b al-Ansari passed by them, so Ibn 'Abbas called him, saying: "O Abu al-Tufayl, come to us, for my companion and I have disputed regarding the companion of Musa whom he sought the way to meet. Did you hear the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) mentioning his affair?" Ubayy said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) saying: "While Musa was among an assembly of the Children of Israel, a man came to him and said: 'Do you know anyone more knowledgeable than you?' Musa said: 'No.' So Allah revealed to Musa: 'Nay, rather Our servant al-Khadir.' He said: So Musa asked the way to meet him, and Allah made the fish a sign for him, and it was said to him: 'When you lose the fish, turn back, for you will meet him.' So Musa traveled as long as Allah willed that he travel, then he said to his young companion: 'Bring us our morning meal.' Musa's young companion said when he asked him for the morning meal: 'Did you see when we took refuge at the rock? Indeed, I forgot the fish, and none made me forget to mention it except Satan.' Musa said to his young companion: 'That is what we were seeking.' So they retraced their footprints, following their tracks, and found Khadir. And there occurred between them what Allah related in His Book." Except that Yunus said: "And he was following the trace of the fish in the sea."

And 'Amr al-Naqid narrated to us, Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from 'Amr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, that the Prophet (pbuh) recited: "You could have taken a payment for it (la-takhidhta 'alayhi ajra)."

And 'Abdullah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Darimi narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us; (H) and 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us, 'Ubaydullah ibn Musa informed us—both of them from Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, with the chain of narration of al-Taymi from Abu Ishaq, similar to his hadith.
